cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in a dataset; a dataset can have no mode, one mode (unimodal), or multiple modes (bimodal or multimodal).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The mode is the only average that can be used for qualitative (categorical) data, since it does not require numerical values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The median is the middle value when all data are arranged in order; for n values, the median position is at (n + 1) ÷ 2.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: For an even number of data values, the median is the mean of the two middle values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The mean (arithmetic mean) = sum of all values ÷ number of values; it uses every data value and is affected by outliers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The weighted mean multiplies each value by its weight, sums these products, then divides by the sum of the weights: x̄ = Σ(wx) ÷ Σw.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The geometric mean of n values is the nth root of their product: GM = ⁿ√(x₁ × x₂ × … × xₙ); it is used for data that grows multiplicatively such as percentage changes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: For grouped data, the estimated mean uses midpoints of each class interval: estimated mean = Σ(f × midpoint) ÷ Σf.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: The mean is affected by extreme values (outliers), whereas the median and mode are not; this is important when choosing which average to use.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: Use the median when data is skewed or contains outliers; use the mean when data is roughly symmetric with no extreme values.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: Use the mode when data is categorical or when you need the most common value; use the weighted mean when values have different levels of importance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Measures Central Tendency
cards.back: When comparing distributions, always state which average you are using and justify your choice.

cards.back: 1. For Measures of Central Tendency questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2.
